title: Presenting an Idea
description: Use structured presentation language to structure, justify, and negotiate ideas related to presenting an idea with appropriate B2 complexity.
objectives: Use structured presentation language to structure, justify, and negotiate ideas related to presenting an idea with appropriate B2 complexity.

stages.title: Understand meaning and form
stages.instructions: Read the concept, pattern, examples, contrast, common issue, and recap.

blocks.text: The communicative aim of this lesson is to use structured presentation language to structure, justify, and negotiate ideas related to presenting an idea with appropriate B2 complexity. The central language focus is structured presentation language. In the context of professional communication, form and meaning work together: first identify the relationship between the ideas, then choose wording that makes that relationship clear to another person. At B2, organize the message so the listener can follow the claim, support, qualification, and practical consequence. Choose collocations and discourse markers that sound natural in professional and social contexts.

blocks.english: A clear explanation addresses keep to the agenda directly.
blocks.explanation: This model establishes the main communicative move.

blocks.english: The speaker emphasized outline a proposal.
blocks.explanation: This model develops or qualifies the message.

blocks.text: Start with the model “A clear explanation addresses keep to the agenda directly.” It establishes a useful direction for the exchange. The second model, “The speaker emphasized outline a proposal.” adds another layer: a reason, implication, contrast, or response. Notice how each complete chunk does a communicative job. Practice replacing one detail while preserving the original grammar, stance, and register. Then connect the revised sentence to a relevant consequence or example instead of changing topic abruptly.

A useful pattern for this lesson is: structured presentation language. Use it when the situation genuinely calls for that meaning. Contrast matters: a direct factual statement presents information, while a qualified or hypothetical form changes the speaker's commitment to it. The choice should be driven by evidence, time reference, relationship, and purpose. In listening, pay attention not only to individual words but also to linkers, stress, and the speaker's degree of certainty.

blocks.title: Contrast
blocks.text: Compare a direct statement with language shaped by structured presentation language; the intended meaning determines the form.

A common issue is to select an advanced-looking form without maintaining its meaning across the sentence. That can create a mismatch in time, stance, or register. Check three things: what happened or is being proposed, how certain the speaker is, and what response is expected. For presenting an idea, clarity comes from a coherent message rather than maximum complexity. The later stages recycle the same vocabulary and expressions so that recognition becomes controlled production and then flexible interaction.

blocks.title: Common issue
blocks.text: Do not add complexity that changes the time reference, degree of certainty, or relationship with the listener.

In the conversation, listen, respond, clarify, and develop the same topic.

stages.title: Listen for meaning and stance
stages.instructions: Listen first, then reveal the text and notice connections, register, and emphasis.

segments.text: To begin with, A clear explanation addresses keep to the agenda directly. The speaker emphasized outline a proposal.
In this situation, The speaker emphasized outline a proposal. Our response should account for main benefit.
From another perspective, Our response should account for main benefit. I take your point.
More specifically, I take your point. I have some reservations.
Even so, I have some reservations. The discussion highlighted find common ground.
As a result, The discussion highlighted find common ground. A clear explanation addresses workable compromise directly.
